_comment: THE REAL CORPUS. Transcribed off 32 slides of actual @drillr_app posts,
2026-05-30 to 2026-06-27, supplied by tomek 2026-08-29. These are not
invented exemplars - every line here went out on the account.
`examples` is injected into the system prompt as THE TARGET VOICE. `archive`
is NOT injected: it is history we keep but do not want copied. Nothing reads
`archive` at runtime, so moving an entry between the two keys is the whole
mechanism for turning a pattern on or off.
This is the highest-leverage file in the repo: the model copies rhythm from
examples far more reliably than it follows an adjective in a rule.
WHAT THE CORPUS SHOWS - and it contradicted the original prompt:
1. NOT ONE item is position-specific. The content slides are broad football
mentality and lifestyle - sleep, food, motivation, work ethic, fear,
comparison. The POSITIONING lives entirely in the fixed app slide ('made
for your position'). Content buys reach, the CTA does the selling. The old
prompt demanded position-specific conditioning in every item, which is why
its drafts never sounded like the account.
2. Two hook formulas, both career-stakes, nothing else: the THREAT ('will
kill your football career', 'never go pro') and the PROOF ('signs that you
will go pro'). No tips, no how-tos, no listicles about drills.
3. ONE item shape: the bare habit, 22-50 characters, no colon. See `archive`
below for the shape that was tried and dropped.
4. The account mixes gerunds ('Eating junk food') and second person ('You
skip stretching') freely inside one set. That is not sloppiness to fix.
5. Items are allowed to be moral and abstract. 'You have talent but no work
ethic' is a real post. The line the corpus never crosses is the bare TRAIT
label - it always names a behaviour, never 'you lack discipline'.
6. Hooks REPEAT. 'kill-career' ran twice, 2026-05-30 and 2026-06-16, with a
different set of items each time. Reusing a hook is normal practice here,
which is what config.copy.repeatHooks encodes.
⚠️ The `caption` fields are NOT transcribed - the export was slides only, no
post text. They are filled with the config.json default so the shape of the
example is complete. Replace them the moment you have the real captions,
because right now they teach the model that every caption is 'lock in'.
A sixth carousel (2026-05-30, same hook as 'kill-career') was in the folder
with its item 1 slide missing, so it is not included. Its app slide read
'Tip: that's why I started using Drillr to track my nutrition and training to
stay locked in' - a first-person testimonial variant of the CTA now pinned in
config.json. Worth knowing that variant existed if the CTA is ever revisited.
itemCount: these all carry five items because config.itemCount is 5. If you
change that, the prompt still asks for the right number - the examples are
allowed to disagree and the prompt says so explicitly.

examples.hook: 5 things that will kill your football career
items: Not getting enough sleep
Eating a lot junk food
You only train when you're motivated
You skip exercising and stretching
Comparing yourself to others
examples.caption: lock in

examples.hook: 5 reasons you will never go pro in football
items: You only train when you feel like it
You blame everyone else for your mistakes
You have talent but no work ethic
You skip stretching and recovery
You always play it safe because you're scared
examples.caption: lock in

examples.hook: 5 signs that you will go pro in football
items: You train even if you're not motivated
You watch football to learn not just for fun
You care about your diet and recovery
You train your weaknesses not just your strengths
You analyse your performance after a match/training
examples.caption: lock in

_archive_comment: ⛔ NOT injected into the prompt. Kept as a record of what ran, not as a
The 'label and cost' shape - '<habit>: <what it costs you>' - ran once, on
2026-05-31. tomek ruled it out on 2026-08-29: item slides carry the bare
habit and no colon. Two reasons it does not work here. The consequence half
roughly doubles the line, and the renderer auto-fits, so the type lands at
about half the size of a short item. And it needs 5-6 lines where render.py
caps at MAX_LINES = 4, so it cannot render the way it originally posted
`lint` now warns on any colon in an item, so this cannot creep back in
unnoticed. To restore the shape: move this entry into `examples`, drop the
colon check in lib/houserules.mjs, put the LABEL AND COST block back in the
system prompt, and raise MAX_LINES to 6 in render.py.

archive.shape: label and cost - RETIRED, do not copy
archive.hook: Small habits that are holding you back from improving
items: Gooning Kills motivation, makes you feel like your goals are boring and worthless
Not getting enough sleep: Ruins your recovery and makes you disoriented and less productive
Eating junk food: Slows muscle growth
Not warming up properly: You risk getting an injury and it reduces your strength
Comparing yourself to others: Destroys your confidence which leads to poor performance
archive.caption: lock in
